Dense hot branch is entered only when input.is_contiguous() and not input.is_conj(). It allocates a fresh destination solely as the Triton flat-copy target; both the copy kernel and the conjugate kernel address the output by flat element offset from out.data_ptr(), so only contiguousness (not a particular stride spelling) affects correctness.

The dense branch passes memory_format=torch.contiguous_format to torch.empty_like. For an already-contiguous, dense, non-overlapping input, torch.empty_like default memory_format=preserve_format yields a tensor with the input's strides, i.e. the same contiguous layout; the keyword is therefore redundant here. Default still allocates independent storage.

preserve_format is documented to copy input strides when the input is non-overlapping and dense; a standard contiguous tensor is non-overlapping and dense, so default empty_like output is contiguous. Removing the explicit contiguous_format keyword does not change contiguity, independent allocation, or the real Triton copy.
